headline: Starlink service restored in Ukraine after 10-day disruption
summary: SpaceX appears to have lifted restrictions on the military-grade Starshield system, following reports of drone control loss and potential intervention from former President Trump.
details: SpaceX has seemingly restored normal Starshield service in Ukraine, the military-grade version of Starlink, after a 10-day period of connectivity issues. The Ukrainian military is still conducting tests to confirm full functionality.

During the disruption, Ukrainian drones lost internet connectivity when flying at speeds around 100 mph, leading to loss of control and increased vulnerability. This period reportedly prompted intervention from former President Donald Trump, who contacted SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.

The restrictions followed previous reports that Musk had ordered SpaceX to throttle Ukraine's Starlink access. Musk stated that Ukraine had violated terms of service by using the system for offensive drone strikes.
Musk previously stated that "Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately," emphasizing the critical role of the service in the ongoing conflict.

topic: pennsylvania mandates labels for ai-generated ads
headline: Pennsylvania requires labels on AI-generated ads
summary: The new AI Deceptive Advertising Act mandates disclosures for AI-modified or generated content, affecting everything from TV commercials to restaurant flyers.
details: Pennsylvania has become one of the first states to enact legislation requiring disclosures on AI-generated advertisements. Governor Josh Shapiro signed the Artificial Intelligence Deceptive Advertising Act into law on Thursday.

The law mandates that any advertisement, including still images, video, audio, or text, that has been 'significantly modified or generated by artificial intelligence' must carry a label in the same format as the ad itself.

This requirement applies broadly, covering major television commercials from large corporations as well as smaller, local advertisements like restaurant flyers. The law's reach extends to ads intended for Pennsylvania, regardless of where they were created.

However, the act contains several loopholes. The definition of 'significantly modified' is subjective, and content intended for 'parody, satire, commentary or criticism,' or anything 'evidently fictional,' is exempt. The interpretation of 'evidently fictional' and what constitutes a 'false consumer perception' remains unclear, leaving room for ambiguity in enforcement.
